title: Hubble: Repair and Scientific Inference
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
A telescope above most of Earth's atmosphere avoids atmospheric blurring and gains access to wavelengths that the atmosphere partly or wholly blocks. That advantage does not eliminate every limitation: mirror shape, detector noise, pointing, calibration, and data analysis still matter. When the Hubble Space Telescope began returning images after its 1990 launch, the repeated blur across instruments pointed investigators toward the optical system rather than a single camera.

The investigation found that the primary mirror had been polished with extraordinary smoothness but to the wrong curvature. A faulty test setup had allowed a precise manufacturing process to converge on an incorrect target. This distinction matters. Precision is the consistency of a process or measurement; accuracy is closeness to the intended or true value. Repeating a biased procedure can produce highly precise error.

Astronauts did not reshape the mirror in orbit. During the first servicing mission in 1993, they installed instruments and corrective optics designed around the measured aberration. The correction worked because engineers could characterize the error and introduce an opposing optical effect. The rescue therefore depended on diagnosis, modular design, accessible components, training, and verification—not on inspiration alone. Later servicing missions replaced or upgraded instruments and extended the observatory's scientific life.

Hubble's deep observations transformed apparently sparse sky into evidence of vast galaxy populations and supplied measurements used in studies of stellar evolution, galaxies, black holes, and cosmic expansion. Yet an image does not announce its own conclusion. Exposure selection, calibration, redshift estimates, distance indicators, comparison with models, and observations from other facilities turn detected light into a scientific claim. Hubble's legacy is both astronomical and methodological: durable knowledge came from a repairable instrument embedded in a wider community of measurement.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Space removes every source of observational error.

options.label: B
options.text: Hubble's scientific value came from optical repair, testable inference, and a wider measurement system.

options.label: C
options.text: Astronauts polished the primary mirror into a new shape in orbit.

options.label: D
options.text: A deep image proves a cosmological theory without calibration.

questions.answer: 正解：B。本文は光学的修正、検証可能な診断、較正や他施設を含む測定共同体を結び付けます。Aは残存誤差、Cは補償光学、Dは画像から主張への推論を誤ります。

questions.prompt: How did similar blur across multiple instruments narrow the possible cause?

options.label: A
options.text: A repeated pattern across separate cameras made a shared upstream optical component more likely than independent camera failures.

options.label: B
options.text: It proved that every detector had failed independently in exactly the same way.

options.label: C
options.text: It showed that the atmosphere was blurring a telescope already above most of it.

options.label: D
options.text: It eliminated the need to investigate the primary mirror or optical path.

questions.answer: 正解：A。別々の装置に共通する像の変形は、個別カメラより共通して光が通る上流の光学系を疑わせます。B～Dは共通原因による診断と逆です。

questions.prompt: The phrase “converge on an incorrect target” is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: vary randomly around the correct value

options.label: B
options.text: consistently approach a value defined by a biased setup

options.label: C
options.text: abandon measurement and rely on imagination

options.label: D
options.text: correct the target by repeating the same test

questions.answer: 正解：B。基準設定が偏っていれば、ばらつきの小さい工程でも同じ誤った値へ近づきます。Aはランダム誤差、Cは測定放棄、Dは反復で系統誤差が消えるとの誤解です。

questions.prompt: How does the primary-mirror case illustrate the difference between precision and accuracy?

options.label: A
options.text: The polishing was smooth and consistent, so precision was high, but the target curvature was wrong, so accuracy was low.

options.label: B
options.text: The mirror had random roughness but the correct curvature, making accuracy and precision identical.

options.label: C
options.text: Accuracy means consistency, while precision means closeness to the intended value.

options.label: D
options.text: A precise process cannot produce an inaccurate result.

questions.answer: 正解：A。工程の一貫性・鏡面の滑らかさは高精度でも、目標曲率が誤っていたため正確さは低い状態でした。Cは定義を逆にし、B・Dは事例と矛盾します。

questions.prompt: Why is the 1993 repair better described as compensating for a known error rather than removing it?

options.label: A
options.text: The original mirror shape remained, while added optics introduced an opposing effect based on the measured aberration.

options.label: B
options.text: Astronauts reshaped and repolished the primary mirror in orbit.

options.label: C
options.text: Engineers ignored the measured aberration and replaced every part at random.

options.label: D
options.text: The repair improved the mirror's original curvature without adding optics.

questions.answer: 正解：A。主鏡の物理形状は残り、測定済み収差と反対方向の光学効果を追加して出力像を補正しました。B～Dは修理方法を誤ります。

questions.prompt: Which statement is best supported by the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Repairability has no scientific value once an instrument is launched.

options.label: B
options.text: A modular instrument can convert diagnosis into replacement, correction, and later upgrade.

options.label: C
options.text: Heroic effort makes calibration unnecessary.

options.label: D
options.text: The mirror flaw prevented all useful work before repair.

questions.answer: 正解：B。モジュール設計とアクセス可能な部品が、診断を修正・交換・更新へ変えました。Aは整備成果、Cは測定と検証、Dは修理前の能力を過度に単純化します。

questions.prompt: Which set lists processes that turn detected light into a scientific claim?

options.label: A
options.text: Exposure selection, calibration, redshift estimates, distance indicators, model comparison, and observations from other facilities

options.label: B
options.text: Image publication alone, without calibration or comparison

options.label: C
options.text: Mirror launch, astronaut inspiration, and public popularity only

options.label: D
options.text: Assuming that every visible feature announces its own interpretation

questions.answer: 正解：A。本文が挙げる露光選択、較正、赤方偏移、距離指標、モデル比較、他施設観測が光を主張へ変えます。B～Dは推論手続を省略します。

questions.prompt: What general lesson follows from “Repeating a biased procedure can produce highly precise error”?

options.label: A
options.text: Reproducibility alone does not guarantee correctness; independent standards, different measurement principles, and calibration histories are needed to detect systematic error.

options.label: B
options.text: A repeated result is always accurate even when the setup is biased.

options.label: C
options.text: Random repetition automatically removes every systematic error.

options.label: D
options.text: Calibration should be avoided when results are consistent.

questions.answer: 正解：A。再現性は真値への近さを保証しないため、独立基準、異なる原理、較正履歴で系統誤差を調べます。B～Dは精度と正確さを混同します。

questions.prompt: Which design policy best reflects the passage's lesson about repairability in costly scientific instruments?

options.label: A
options.text: Compare fault risks with the mass and cost of service interfaces, preserve diagnostic data, and use modularity, redundancy, or servicing when their scientific benefit justifies the tradeoff.

options.label: B
options.text: Make every component serviceable regardless of added failure modes or mission needs.

options.label: C
options.text: Reject all repair options because launched instruments have no further scientific value.

options.label: D
options.text: Ignore diagnostic information and rely on inspiration after a failure.

questions.answer: 正解：A。修理可能性を科学性能として評価しつつ、質量・費用・故障モードとのトレードオフを比較する案です。Bは無条件化し、C・Dは診断と延命の価値を否定します。
